newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin Nazi bunker ready for demolition.
newsitem.headline: Berlin Nazi bunker ready for demolition.

text.p: Explosives experts began preparations on Monday to demolish a World War Two bunker that may have been used by Adolf Hitler's close aide Albert Speer to make way for a new office building.

The concrete bunker located next to the Brandenburg Gate was unearthed in December by workers who are building a regional office for DG Bank. Historians say it may have been used by Speer, Hitler's armaments minister and architect.

"Our experts looked inside the bunker today to decide where to start drilling and inserting the explosives," said Christian Schilling, a spokesman for DG Bank in Berlin. "If all goes as planned, we will blow it up on Tuesday."

Construction workers found six and a half tonnes of live and defused grenades and other ammunition along with cots, cutlery and telephones in the 225 square metre (2,400 square foot) subterranean complex.
The ammunition was disposed of at the weekend but DG Bank plans to keep other objects retrieved from the bunker for display at its current Berlin office.

Speer remained at Hitler's side until escaping shortly before the end of the war. He was later convicted of war crimes in Nuremberg and sentenced to 20 years in prison, which he served in Berlin's Spandau prison.
Schilling said the bunker was found one and a half metres (five feet) below the Pariser Platz, between the Academy of Arts and a plot reserved for the new U.S. embassy.
Historians say the bunker could be one of at least six wartime bunkers under Pariser Platz near the site where Hitler's chancellery once stood.
